what: Redraws the photo in WebGL and scatters the edges as if smudged with a brush. A horizontally long brush-grain noise (5×16) and a cloud noise (3×) are added to the distance from the edge and cut at a threshold, and the cut border is pushed outward by 7% of the noise and smeared. On reveal the threshold recedes from center to outside in 1.6s expo-out so the photo blooms from the inside, and even when fully revealed the outer 6% of the edge stays as brush marks that ripple slowly. With look: blob, it takes a round blob shape instead of a rectangle.

options.on: view (when it enters the screen · default) · hover (hover over the parent — or an ancestor chosen with host — to open, release to retract — photo behind a list row) · load (right on attach) · manual (when fx:play is sent to the element — first photo after the loader)
options.host: on: for hover, the ancestor css to hover over (e.g. .row), default parent
options.rest: Brush stroke width left when fully bloomed, default .06
options.opacity: Overall panel opacity, default 1 — photo behind list rows uses .65 to sink into the background
options.look: If blob, a round blotch shape (next work square photo)
options.[data-fx-part=photo]: Grill (same source) — if missing, bakes a placeholder graphic with data-label over a garment-color mist

from.where: list.html Work row background photo (.row-photo, on: hover) · detail.html head photo (.hero-photo) · next Work (.next-photo, look: blob) — original WebGL photo plane (edges carved with displacement/fbm-mask·02 brush texture)

note: The original uses brush-grain and noise texture images as masks — here a shader noise produces the same grain. Each panel uses one WebGL context, so do not place more than 10 on one screen (list rows are hover type, so only the hovered one is drawn)
